note: Set A correctly captures the U = 10 m/s normal-force peak (~11,000 N/m near 0.85 m span), the zero normal force at the root, and the design-point thrust coefficient of 0.900 at 0° pitch / TSR 9, with wind speed and span conditions kept on the force readings. Set B twice binds the ~11,000 N/m peak to U = 9 m/s (it is the U = 10 curve, U = 9 peaks near 8,500 N/m) and twice reports power-coefficient contour values (0.480, 0.420) as thrust coefficients, plus inflated tangential maxima for U = 8 and U = 9 and a too-low 150 N/m at U = 6. Set A's main flaws are four claims with invented 'series 1–4' conditions and two over-stated normal-force values (6,800 N/m at U = 7, 8,500 N/m at U = 8). Both sets read contour values only approximately, but A misreads fewer curves and misbinds fewer properties.
